List every `scripts/*` file with a one-line purpose.

Report concisely, grouped by the five headings. File paths for everything. Do not read large source files in full — I only need the inventory and mechanics.

=== SCOPE-CHECK ===
---
name: scope-check
description: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
---

Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs.

The prompt to check is: $ARGUMENTS

## What to do

1. **Identify every file the prompt would likely touch** — both files named explicitly and files Claude would naturally reach through refactoring upward, shared imports, or "while I'm in here" changes.

2. **Classify each file by tier**:
   - Tier 1 (Frozen) — see [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md)
   - Tier 2 (Protected) — see [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md)
   - Tier 3 (Squad-owned) — see `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` *(if absent, infer from path: checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B)*
   - Tier 4 (Feature-local, safe)

3. **Assess the risk**:
   - Is the prompt open-ended in a way that lets Claude drift into shared code?
   - Could Claude refactor upward into hooks or utilities not mentioned?
   - Does it cross squad boundaries (Squad A territory + Squad B territory in the same prompt)?
   - Does it name specific files, or just a feature area?

4. **Verdict**: output one of:
   - ✅ SAFE — clearly scoped, no Tier 1 or 2 risk
   - ⚠️ RISKY — likely to drift, needs a rewrite before running
   - 🚫 BLOCKED — requires Tier 1 modification, stop and get owner approval first

5. **If RISKY or BLOCKED**, rewrite the prompt so it is safely scoped:
   - Name exact file paths under `overrides/app/...`
   - End with "Do not modify any other files"
   - Split cross-squad work into two separate prompts

## Output format

Use a compact table for the file/tier list. One short paragraph for the verdict. If rewriting, show the improved prompt in a code block.

=== CODE-QUALITY ===
---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

The component name is: $ARGUMENTS

## Conventions

Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) (naming, folder layout,
cross-cutting rules), [components.md](../../rules/components.md) (props types, JSDoc policy,
composition, Storybook categorisation), and [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra token usage)

scaffolding.

- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).

## Steps

1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage.    - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).

#!/bin/bash

# Ralph Loop Stop Hook
# Prevents session exit when a ralph-loop is active
# Feeds Claude's output back as input to continue the loop

set -euo pipefail

# Read hook input from stdin (advanced stop hook API)
HOOK_INPUT=$(cat)

# Check if ralph-loop is active
RALPH_STATE_FILE=".claude/ralph-loop.local.md"

if [[ ! -f "$RALPH_STATE_FILE" ]]; then
  # No active loop - allow exit
  exit 0
fi

# Parse markdown frontmatter (YAML between ---) and extract values
FRONTMATTER=$(sed -n '/^---$/,/^---$/{ /^---$/d; p; }' "$RALPH_STATE_FILE")
ITERATION=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^iteration:' | sed 's/iteration: *//')
MAX_ITERATIONS=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^max_iterations:' | sed 's/max_iterations: *//')
# Extract completion_promise and strip surrounding quotes if present
COMPLETION_PROMISE=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^completion_promise:' | sed 's/completion_promise: *//' | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')

# Session isolation: the state file is project-scoped, but the Stop hook
# fires in every Claude Code session in that project. If another session
# started the loop, this session must not block (or touch the state file).
# Legacy state files without session_id fall through (preserves old behavior).
STATE_SESSION=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^session_id:' | sed 's/session_id: *//' || true)
HOOK_SESSION=$(echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | jq -r '.session_id // ""')
if [[ -n "$STATE_SESSION" ]] && [[ "$STATE_SESSION" != "$HOOK_SESSION" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Validate numeric fields before arithmetic operations
if [[ ! "$ITERATION" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: State file corrupted" >&2
  echo "   File: $RALPH_STATE_FILE" >&2
  echo "   Problem: 'iteration' field is not a valid number (got: '$ITERATION')" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   This usually means the state file was manually edited or corrupted." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping. Run /ralph-loop again to start fresh." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ ! "$MAX_ITERATIONS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: State file corrupted" >&2
  echo "   File: $RALPH_STATE_FILE" >&2
  echo "   Problem: 'max_iterations' field is not a valid number (got: '$MAX_ITERATIONS')" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   This usually means the state file was manually edited or corrupted." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping. Run /ralph-loop again to start fresh." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Check if max iterations reached
if [[ $MAX_ITERATIONS -gt 0 ]] && [[ $ITERATION -ge $MAX_ITERATIONS ]]; then
  echo "🛑 Ralph loop: Max iterations ($MAX_ITERATIONS) reached."
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Get transcript path from hook input
TRANSCRIPT_PATH=$(echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | jq -r '.transcript_path')

if [[ ! -f "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH" ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Transcript file not found" >&2
  echo "   Expected: $TRANSCRIPT_PATH" >&2
  echo "   This is unusual and may indicate a Claude Code internal issue." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Read last assistant message from transcript (JSONL format - one JSON per line)
# First check if there are any assistant messages
if ! grep -q '"role":"assistant"' "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH"; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: No assistant messages found in transcript" >&2
  echo "   Transcript: $TRANSCRIPT_PATH" >&2
  echo "   This is unusual and may indicate a transcript format issue" >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Extract the most recent assistant text block.
#
# Claude Code writes each content block (text/tool_use/thinking) as its own
# JSONL line, all with role=assistant. So slurp the last N assistant lines,
# flatten to text blocks only, and take the last one.
#
# Capped at the last 100 assistant lines to keep jq's slurp input bounded
# for long-running sessions.
LAST_LINES=$(grep '"role":"assistant"' "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH" | tail -n 100)
if [[ -z "$LAST_LINES" ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Failed to extract assistant messages" >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Parse the recent lines and pull out the final text block.
# `last // ""` yields empty string when no text blocks exist (e.g. a turn
# that is all tool calls). That's fine: empty text means no <promise> tag,
# so the loop simply continues.
# (Briefly disable errexit so a jq failure can be caught by the $? check.)
set +e
LAST_OUTPUT=$(echo "$LAST_LINES" | jq -rs '
  map(.message.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text) | last // ""
' 2>&1)
JQ_EXIT=$?
set -e

# Check if jq succeeded
if [[ $JQ_EXIT -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Failed to parse assistant message JSON" >&2
  echo "   Error: $LAST_OUTPUT" >&2
  echo "   This may indicate a transcript format issue." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Check for completion promise (only if set)
if [[ "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" != "null" ]] && [[ -n "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" ]]; then
  # Extract text from <promise> tags using Perl for multiline support
  # -0777 slurps entire input, s flag makes . match newlines
  # .*? is non-greedy (takes FIRST tag), whitespace normalized
  PROMISE_TEXT=$(echo "$LAST_OUTPUT" | perl -0777 -pe 's/.*?<promise>(.*?)<\/promise>.*/$1/s; s/^\s+|\s+$//g; s/\s+/ /g' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

  # Use = for literal string comparison (not pattern matching)
  # == in [[ ]] does glob pattern matching which breaks with *, ?, [ characters
  if [[ -n "$PROMISE_TEXT" ]] && [[ "$PROMISE_TEXT" = "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" ]]; then
    echo "✅ Ralph loop: Detected <promise>$COMPLETION_PROMISE</promise>"
    rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Not complete - continue loop with SAME PROMPT
NEXT_ITERATION=$((ITERATION + 1))

# Extract prompt (everything after the closing ---)
# Skip first --- line, skip until second --- line, then print everything after

#!/bin/bash

# Ralph Loop Stop Hook
# Prevents session exit when a ralph-loop is active
# Feeds Claude's output back as input to continue the loop

set -euo pipefail

# Read hook input from stdin (advanced stop hook API)
HOOK_INPUT=$(cat)

# Check if ralph-loop is active
RALPH_STATE_FILE=".claude/ralph-loop.local.md"

if [[ ! -f "$RALPH_STATE_FILE" ]]; then
  # No active loop - allow exit
  exit 0
fi

# Parse markdown frontmatter (YAML between ---) and extract values
FRONTMATTER=$(sed -n '/^---$/,/^---$/{ /^---$/d; p; }' "$RALPH_STATE_FILE")
ITERATION=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^iteration:' | sed 's/iteration: *//')
MAX_ITERATIONS=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^max_iterations:' | sed 's/max_iterations: *//')
# Extract completion_promise and strip surrounding quotes if present
COMPLETION_PROMISE=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^completion_promise:' | sed 's/completion_promise: *//' | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')

# Session isolation: the state file is project-scoped, but the Stop hook
# fires in every Claude Code session in that project. If another session
# started the loop, this session must not block (or touch the state file).
# Legacy state files without session_id fall through (preserves old behavior).
STATE_SESSION=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^session_id:' | sed 's/session_id: *//' || true)
HOOK_SESSION=$(echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | jq -r '.session_id // ""')
if [[ -n "$STATE_SESSION" ]] && [[ "$STATE_SESSION" != "$HOOK_SESSION" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Validate numeric fields before arithmetic operations
if [[ ! "$ITERATION" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: State file corrupted" >&2
  echo "   File: $RALPH_STATE_FILE" >&2
  echo "   Problem: 'iteration' field is not a valid number (got: '$ITERATION')" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   This usually means the state file was manually edited or corrupted." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping. Run /ralph-loop again to start fresh." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ ! "$MAX_ITERATIONS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: State file corrupted" >&2
  echo "   File: $RALPH_STATE_FILE" >&2
  echo "   Problem: 'max_iterations' field is not a valid number (got: '$MAX_ITERATIONS')" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   This usually means the state file was manually edited or corrupted." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping. Run /ralph-loop again to start fresh." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Check if max iterations reached
if [[ $MAX_ITERATIONS -gt 0 ]] && [[ $ITERATION -ge $MAX_ITERATIONS ]]; then
  echo "🛑 Ralph loop: Max iterations ($MAX_ITERATIONS) reached."
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Get transcript path from hook input
TRANSCRIPT_PATH=$(echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | jq -r '.transcript_path')

if [[ ! -f "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH" ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Transcript file not found" >&2
  echo "   Expected: $TRANSCRIPT_PATH" >&2
  echo "   This is unusual and may indicate a Claude Code internal issue." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Read last assistant message from transcript (JSONL format - one JSON per line)
# First check if there are any assistant messages
if ! grep -q '"role":"assistant"' "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH"; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: No assistant messages found in transcript" >&2
  echo "   Transcript: $TRANSCRIPT_PATH" >&2
  echo "   This is unusual and may indicate a transcript format issue" >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

# Extract the most recent assistant text block.
#
# Claude Code writes each content block (text/tool_use/thinking) as its own
# JSONL line, all with role=assistant. So slurp the last N assistant lines,
# flatten to text blocks only, and take the last one.
#
# Capped at the last 100 assistant lines to keep jq's slurp input bounded
# for long-running sessions.
LAST_LINES=$(grep '"role":"assistant"' "$TRANSCRIPT_PATH" | tail -n 100)
if [[ -z "$LAST_LINES" ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Failed to extract assistant messages" >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0

# `last // ""` yields empty string when no text blocks exist (e.g. a turn
# that is all tool calls). That's fine: empty text means no <promise> tag,
# so the loop simply continues.
# (Briefly disable errexit so a jq failure can be caught by the $? check.)
set +e
LAST_OUTPUT=$(echo "$LAST_LINES" | jq -rs '
  map(.message.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text) | last // ""
' 2>&1)
JQ_EXIT=$?
set -e

if [[ $JQ_EXIT -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "⚠️  Ralph loop: Failed to parse assistant message JSON" >&2
  echo "   Error: $LAST_OUTPUT" >&2
  echo "   This may indicate a transcript format issue." >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0

if [[ "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" != "null" ]] && [[ -n "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" ]]; then
  # Extract text from <promise> tags using Perl for multiline support

  PROMISE_TEXT=$(echo "$LAST_OUTPUT" | perl -0777 -pe 's/.*?<promise>(.*?)<\/promise>.*/$1/s; s/^\s+|\s+$//g; s/\s+/ /g' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

    rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
    exit 0
  fi

NEXT_ITERATION=$((ITERATION + 1))

# Extract prompt (everything after the closing ---)
# Skip first --- line, skip until second --- line, then print everything after
# Use i>=2 instead of i==2 to handle --- in prompt content
PROMPT_TEXT=$(awk '/^---$/{i++; next} i>=2' "$RALPH_STATE_FILE")

  echo "   File: $RALPH_STATE_FILE" >&2
  echo "   Problem: No prompt text found" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   This usually means:" >&2

  echo "     • File was corrupted during writing" >&2
  echo "" >&2
  echo "   Ralph loop is stopping. Run /ralph-loop again to start fresh." >&2
  rm "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi

sed "s/^iteration: .*/iteration: $NEXT_ITERATION/" "$RALPH_STATE_FILE" > "$TEMP_FILE"
mv "$TEMP_FILE" "$RALPH_STATE_FILE"

# Build system message with iteration count and completion promise info
if [[ "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" != "null" ]] && [[ -n "$COMPLETION_PROMISE" ]]; then
  SYSTEM_MSG="🔄 Ralph iteration $NEXT_ITERATION | To stop: output <promise>$COMPLETION_PROMISE</promise> (ONLY when statement is TRUE - do not lie to exit!)"
else
  SYSTEM_MSG="🔄 Ralph iteration $NEXT_ITERATION | No completion promise set - loop runs infinitely"
fi

  }'

# Stop hook: ask Claude to reflect on the session and draft proposals
# for AGENTS.md, .docs/memory/*, and any other docs that may have drifted.
# Proposals are written to .docs/agents-proposals/ — NEVER edits docs directly.

  exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
#
# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
#
# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
#
# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
status=0

while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
  case "$remote_ref" in
    refs/tags/v*)
      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
        status=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
done

exit $status

Inventory complete. Findings below.

---

## 1. Existing agent definitions

**Nothing project-authored. Zero custom agents exist anywhere.**

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/agents/` — **does not exist**
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/agents/` — **does not exist**
- Repo-wide `find -type d -name agents` (excluding `node_modules`) — **no results**. The only `.agents/` dir is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md` (a skill, not an agent — symlinked into `.claude/skills/code-review`).

The only agents on the machine ship with enabled plugins (all under `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/`). Nearest-shaped to your roles:

| Agent | Path | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `code-architect`, `code-explorer`, `code-reviewer` | `feature-dev/unknown/agents/` | architect ≈ planner; reviewer ≈ scorer |
| `code-reviewer`, `pr-test-analyzer`, `silent-failure-hunter`, `type-design-analyzer`, `comment-analyzer`, `code-simplifier` | `pr-review-toolkit/unknown/agents/` | **closest to a scorer panel** — 6 specialised reviewers |
| `agent-sdk-verifier-ts/py` | `agent-sdk-dev/unknown/agents/` | verifier pattern (SDK-specific, not reusable) |
| `code-simplifier` | `code-simplifier/1.0.0/agents/` | quality-only refactor |

**No builder, no tester, no scorer, no orchestrator, no retrospective agent exists.** All five roles are greenfield. I did not read frontmatter model/tools fields for the plugin agents since none are project-owned — say the word if you want those enumerated.

---

## 2. Skills relevant to a build loop

All at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Frontmatter is minimal throughout — only `name` + `description`; **no `allowed-tools`, no `model`, no tool restrictions on any of them.** Every skill takes `$ARGUMENTS`.

### `scope-check` — highest overlap with your orchestrator gate
- **Reads:** `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `protectedFiles.md`, `squadA.md`, `squadB.md`. Falls back to path-inference (checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B) if squad files are absent.
- **Input:** a *prompt string*, not a diff. It predicts files a prompt would touch, including drift ("refactoring upward, shared imports, 'while I'm in here'").
- **Outputs:** a compact file/tier table + a one-verdict paragraph: `SAFE` / `RISKY` / `BLOCKED`. On RISKY/BLOCKED it **rewrites the prompt** into a scoped version (exact `overrides/app/...` paths, appends "Do not modify any other files", splits cross-squad work into two prompts).
- **Writes files:** no.
- **Loop fit:** this is a *pre-flight prompt linter*, not a post-hoc diff checker. Correct call site is orchestrator → **before** dispatching each builder task, feeding it the task prompt. It will not score a completed change. Note `BLOCKED` is defined as "stop and get owner approval" — a human gate that will halt an unattended loop by design.

### `code-quality` — highest overlap with your scorer
- **Reads:** `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `css.md`, `components.md`, `typescript.md`, `testing.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (when present).
- **Input:** a path, or **defaults to `git diff --name-only main`** (note: `main`, whereas `pr-checklist` uses `develop` — inconsistent baseline). Excludes `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `*.stories.tsx`, registry files.
- **Mechanics:** self-fans-out into **4 parallel agents** when >5 files (A naming/structure, B import analysis incl. circular-import detection one level deep and `../../../..` depth >3, C TypeScript, D test/story coverage). ≤5 files runs sequentially in one pass. Runs `npx tsc --noEmit` **once per branch**, not per file.
- **Outputs:** a single prioritised report with fixed sections — `🔴 Must fix before PR merge` / `🟡 Should fix in this PR` / `🔵 Backlog` / `✅ No issues found` / `Summary: X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog`.
- **Writes files:** no — explicitly "read-only diagnostic… Do not modify any files".
- **Loop fit:** the `🔴 count == 0` line is a ready-made numeric pass/fail signal for your scorer. Biggest gap: it is a *convention* auditor, not a *behaviour* auditor — no test execution, no AC verification. Your tester still needs to own `npm run test` / `npm run lint`. Also it already spawns 4 subagents internally, so nesting it inside a scorer subagent gives you two levels of fan-out — budget for that.

### `new-component` — builder helper
Reads a nearby existing component (or a base template from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/`) plus the three rule files. **Writes** `overrides/app/components/<name>/index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, optional `index.test.tsx`. Runs `npx tsc --noEmit`. Hard constraints: must not modify existing files (no route/parent/theme auto-wiring), must not add npm packages, must not import from `node_modules/...` source paths.

### `pr-checklist` — retrospective / hand-off helper
Step 1 **invokes `/code-quality`** (nested skill call — mind the fan-out). Runs `git diff --name-only develop`, tiers each file, detects cross-squad PRs. Outputs a copy-paste PR description: summary bullets, file/tier/owner/reviewer table, required pre-merge actions, CodeRabbit gates (Conventional Commits title, Jira URL, JSDoc), test checklist. **Writes files:** no, and explicitly nothing is posted for you. Contains a hard constraint relevant to your tester: **"Claude must not start the dev server"** — `npm start` is a human action.

### `session-start` — orchestrator bootstrap
Sequential 5-step ritual. Reads in parallel: `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, `sprintScope.md`, `feedback.md`, `upstreamBaseline.md`, and `.claude/session-notes.md`. Runs `git branch --show-current` (**hard stop if `develop`/`main`**), reads `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` if on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`, runs `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh`. Ends by **asking the user to confirm direction** — a blocking human gate, unsuitable inside an unattended loop as written. **Writes:** may write `.claude/session-notes.md` (gitignored, per-developer, the one Claude-writable memory file). Also documents the living-memory table: `.docs/memory/*` and `.claude/rules/*` are human-owned/Tier 1, Claude must not edit them directly.

### `qa-generate` — tester scaffolder, human-gated
Three phases. Phase 1 asks 6 questions **one at a time**. Phase 2 **writes** `e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{desc}.feature`, then **hard-stops** and demands Lead QA sign-off before Phase 3 generates the Playwright spec. Requires `e2e/` to already exist or it aborts. Not loop-compatible without stripping the gate.

### `code-review` — external scorer
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md` (symlink target of `.claude/skills/code-review`). Wraps the **CodeRabbit CLI** — checks `coderabbit --version` / `auth status`, requires v0.4.0+ for `--agent` (agent-readable output + fix guidance). Works on staged/committed/all changes, supports base branch selection, groups findings Critical/Warning/Info. Explicitly designed for "autonomous cycles without manual intervention" — the most loop-native scorer already present, but it is a network call on an external CLI.

**Canonical inventory doc:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/README.md` — a table per category with a "Human-in-the-lead checkpoint" column for every skill. Read that column before wiring anything into an unattended loop; **every single skill has one.** (Note: the README documents a `/contentful-drift-check` skill whose directory does not exist.)

---

## 3. Loop / iteration tooling

### `ralph-loop` plugin — enabled and functional
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/1.0.0/`

- Commands: `commands/ralph-loop.md` (`PROMPT [--max-iterations N] [--completion-promise TEXT]`), `commands/cancel-ralph.md`, `commands/help.md`. All three set `hide-from-slash-command-tool: "true"` — **not invocable via the Skill tool, only as a user-typed slash command.**
- Mechanism: `scripts/setup-ralph-loop.sh` writes state to **`.claude/ralph-loop.local.md`** (frontmatter: `iteration`, `max_iterations`, `completion_promise`, `session_id`; body = the prompt). `hooks/stop-hook.sh` registers a **`Stop` hook** that reads the transcript, and returns `{"decision":"block","reason":<prompt>}` to re-feed the identical prompt, incrementing `iteration` in place.
- Exit conditions: `iteration >= max_iterations`; or the last assistant text block contains `<promise>EXACT TEXT</promise>` matching `completion_promise` literally; or state-file corruption / missing transcript (all delete the state file and allow exit).
- Session-isolated via `session_id`, so a loop in one session won't block another.
- **This is your closed-loop driver, already installed.** The `completion_promise` is exactly the "loop until pass" primitive you described.

### `/loop` skill
Listed as available (`loop`: "Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval, e.g. `/loop 5m /foo`; omit the interval to let the model self-pace"). **Not found on disk** under `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/plugins/`, or the CLI install paths — it is a built-in managed skill bundled in the binary. ### Three things I'd flag before you design further

1. **The `Stop`-hook collision (§4) is the blocker.** `session-reflect.sh` blocks exit on any dirty tree and tells Claude to stop working; `ralph-loop`'s hook blocks exit to keep working. They fire on the same turn. Nothing else in this inventory will stop your loop dead the way this will.

Your scorer needs to expect and ignore that churn, and `git add`/`commit`/`push` are not in either allowlist.
3. **Reuse, don't rebuild:** `code-quality` already gives you a fan-out scorer with a numeric `🔴` pass signal, and `scope-check` already gives you a tier-aware pre-flight gate — but note the two are *different phases* (post-hoc diff audit vs. pre-flight prompt lint), and `code-quality`'s baseline is `main` while `pr-checklist`'s is `develop`.
